ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

2. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

4. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

5. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

6. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

7. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. blue
   C. run
   D. happiness

8. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

10. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. going

11. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.

12. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a joining word

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Thank you and Congratulatory notes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Conversational Skills: interviews and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Conversational Skills: interviews and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

2. D — Where is the library?

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

5. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

7. C — run

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

10. B — went

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

12. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Thank you and Congratulatory notes; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Conversational Skills: interviews; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Conversational Skills: interviews; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
